paragraphs.title: God’s Glory in the Heavens and the Sun

easy.explanation: Psalm 19:1 says, “The heavens declare the glory of God.”
The verse says, “Day unto day uttereth speech.”
easy.q: What does day unto day utter?

easy.explanation: The sun is described as “a bridegroom coming out of his chamber.”
easy.q: What is the sun compared to when it comes out?

medium.explanation: The heavens declare God’s glory and the firmament shows His handiwork, even without ordinary speech.
medium.q: How do the heavens and the firmament show God’s glory?

medium.explanation: In this context, “sheweth” means makes known or displays.
medium.q: What does “sheweth” mean in “the firmament sheweth his handywork”?

answers: It moves powerfully along its course
medium.explanation: The sun rejoices “as a strong man to run a race,” emphasizing its vigorous movement.
medium.q: What does the description of the sun as a strong man suggest?

answers: They all communicate knowledge of God’s glory without ordinary speech
They all depend on human words
challenge.explanation: The passage presents them as witnesses that communicate without audible speech or language.
challenge.q: What idea is shared by the day, the night, and the heavens?

answers: Nothing is hidden from the sun’s heat
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the far-reaching power and warmth of the sun.
challenge.q: What does “there is nothing hid from the heat thereof” mean?

answers: It presents the sun as weak and limited
It describes its movement as powerful and far-reaching
It describes the sun as hidden
challenge.explanation: The sun’s course reaches from one end of heaven to the other, displaying great power and scope.
challenge.q: How does the description of the sun strengthen the theme of God’s glory?

paragraphs.title: The Perfection of the Torah and Its Effect on People

easy.explanation: Psalm 19:7 says, “The law of the LORD is perfect.”
easy.q: How is the law of the LORD described?

easy.explanation: The law is described as “converting the soul,” or restoring and turning it.
easy.q: What does the law do to the soul?

easy.explanation: The verse says the commandment is “enlightening the eyes.”
easy.q: What does the commandment of the LORD do to the eyes?

answers: Because they are sure and right, they give wisdom and joy
Because they are hidden, they cause confusion
Because they are brief, they conceal things
medium.explanation: The passage connects the reliability and uprightness of God’s words with wisdom, joy, and understanding.
medium.q: What is the connection between the qualities of God’s words and their effect on people?

medium.explanation: A testimony is a witness or declaration; here it is described as sure, or trustworthy.
medium.q: What does “testimony” mean in “the testimony of the LORD is sure”?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “The judgments of the LORD are true and righteous altogether.”
medium.q: Which quality best describes the judgments of the LORD?

challenge.explanation: The passage describes God’s words as converting the soul, making the simple wise, rejoicing the heart, and enlightening the eyes.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of the effects of God’s words on people?

answers: Because they are valuable and beneficial to people
Because they are made of gold
Because they are spoken only at night
challenge.explanation: The comparisons emphasize the great value and sweetness of God’s words.
challenge.q: Why are God’s judgments described as more desirable than gold and sweeter than honey?

answers: All of the LORD’s judgments are true and righteous
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the complete truth and righteousness of the LORD’s judgments.

paragraphs.title: The Psalmist Facing Errors and Temptations

easy.explanation: He prays, “cleanse thou me from secret faults.”
easy.q: From what does the psalmist say he needs cleansing?

easy.explanation: He asks, “Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to keep him from?

easy.explanation: He asks that presumptuous sins not have dominion over him.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask not to have dominion over him?

answers: A person may err without understanding or recognizing the error
medium.explanation: The question “Who can understand his errors?” recognizes that people may not perceive all their own faults.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask to be cleansed from secret faults?

medium.explanation: Presumptuous sins are committed boldly or arrogantly rather than through simple ignorance.

answers: He may fall away from uprightness
He will run across the heavens
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks for protection so that he may remain upright and innocent from great transgression.
medium.q: What may happen if presumptuous sins have dominion over the psalmist?

answers: He seeks to obey while recognizing human weakness
He rejects the commandments while praising them
He describes the sun while asking it for help
challenge.explanation: He values God’s law but still acknowledges his need for cleansing and protection.
challenge.q: What tension appears in the psalmist’s words?

answers: The person needs cleansing from hidden errors and protection from deliberate wrongdoing
Both express the sweetness of the law
challenge.explanation: The two requests address different dangers that can damage a person’s moral integrity.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between secret faults and presumptuous sins?

answers: To be upright and innocent from great transgression
challenge.explanation: He asks that sin not rule him so that he may be upright and innocent.
challenge.q: What result does the psalmist seek?

paragraphs.title: A Prayer for Words and Thoughts

answers: The words of his mouth and the meditation of his heart
easy.explanation: He prays, “Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask to be acceptable?

easy.explanation: He asks that they be acceptable “in thy sight,” addressing the LORD.
easy.q: In whose sight does the psalmist want his words and thoughts to be acceptable?

easy.explanation: The verse ends, “O LORD, my strength, and my redeemer.”
easy.q: What titles does the psalmist use for the LORD?

answers: Both his spoken words and his inward thoughts
Only the movement of the sun
medium.explanation: He mentions both “the words of my mouth” and “the meditation of my heart.”
medium.q: What does the psalmist’s prayer include?

medium.explanation: Meditation refers to inward thought, reflection, or consideration.
medium.q: What does “meditation” mean in “the meditation of my heart”?

answers: The LORD is the source of power and support
The LORD is a heavenly body
The LORD is a presumptuous man
medium.explanation: Calling the LORD his strength shows dependence on Him for power and stability.
medium.q: What does the title “my strength” express?

answers: He seeks agreement between his outward words and inward thoughts
He wants to describe the sun’s course
He wants to distinguish the law from the commandment
challenge.explanation: The prayer includes both speech and thought, expressing a desire for complete inward and outward integrity.
challenge.q: Why does the psalmist mention both his mouth and his heart?

answers: It asks for God’s help in achieving inward and outward holiness
It returns to the description of the sun’s heat
It removes the need for careful living
challenge.explanation: After asking for cleansing and protection, the psalmist asks that his thoughts and words also be acceptable to God.
challenge.q: How does the conclusion connect with the section about errors and temptations?

answers: The LORD is both the source of power and the one who delivers
The LORD is only a judge
The LORD is only the source of light
challenge.explanation: These titles express the LORD’s sustaining power and His role as the psalmist’s deliverer.
challenge.q: What is the meaning of “my strength, and my redeemer” at the end?
